items.markdown:
If you're looking around **Hull**, I’d be cautious about buying a “blue Staffy” purely from an advert or social-media seller. Blue is a recognised Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour, but health testing and the breeder’s practices matter much more than colour. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Where to start

- **The Kennel Club Find a Puppy** — this is the first place I’d check. You can filter for Staffordshire Bull Terriers, location/distance, health-tested parents and breed-standard colours. [thekennelclub.org.uk](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [RSPCA Hull & East Riding CIO](https://rspcahull.org.uk/) — worth checking if you're open to a young Staffy or Staffy cross rather than specifically a blue pedigree puppy.
- [Oakwood Dog Rescue](http://www.oakwooddogrescue.co.uk/) — another Hull-area rescue worth contacting about Staffy-type dogs.
- I found several businesses advertising Staffies farther away, but I **wouldn't treat their presence in search results as an endorsement**. I'd verify their licensing, health-test records and breeding history before considering them.

### What to ask the breeder

For a Staffordshire Bull Terrier, I'd ask for **actual certificates/results**, rather than accepting “parents are healthy” as an answer.

1. **“Can I see the parents' health-test results?”**

 - Hereditary cataracts (**HC-HSF4**)
- **L-2-HGA**
- Eye examination
- Elbow testing
- Ask for the registered names/numbers so you can independently check the results. The Kennel Club specifically recommends these tests for the breed. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/cvef530x/kc_health_standard_07-25-web.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
2. **“Can I see the puppy with its mother at the place where it was raised?”**
 Don't agree to meet in a car park or have the puppy delivered without seeing where it was bred. The Kennel Club advises buyers to meet the breeder and see both the dam and puppy before committing. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-an-assured-breeder/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **“What is the mother's temperament like? Can I meet her?”**
 Ask about how both parents behave around people, children and other dogs.
4. **“How old will the puppy be when it leaves?”**
 Ask exactly when it can go home, what vaccinations, worming and microchipping it will have had, and what veterinary records you'll receive.
5. **“What socialisation have you been doing?”**
 Ask whether the puppies have experienced household noises, handling, visitors, children, car journeys and other appropriate experiences.
6. **“Why did you choose these two dogs to breed?”**
 A good breeder should be able to explain their breeding goals beyond producing fashionable colours.
7. **“Have you bred blue Staffies before, and have there been skin, coat or other health problems in your lines?”**
 Don't let the attractive colour distract from the wider health history.
8. **“What happens if I can't keep the dog?”**
 A responsible breeder should care about the puppy throughout its life and have a clear return/rehome policy.

### One important blue-Staffy warning

Be particularly wary of adverts emphasising **“rare blue,” “exclusive colour,” “micro blue,” “XL blue,”** etc. Blue itself isn't a disqualifying colour—the Kennel Club lists blue among the Staffordshire Bull Terrier's breed-standard colours. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?gad=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

I'd also avoid anyone who won't let you see the mother, pressures you to pay a deposit immediately, has lots of different breeds/litters available, can't produce health-test documentation, or wants to arrange collection somewhere other than the breeding premises.

If you want, I can **search specifically for currently advertised blue Staffy litters within, say, 50 miles of Hull and separate the potentially reputable ones from the red flags**.
